title: Polynomial-time closure under block search
statement: Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers. For a binary string $z$, let $x$ be the first component of its encoded pair (or the empty string if it does not parse as a pair), and let $y$ be the second component (or the empty string if it does not parse). Set $B=a(|x|+1)^k$, and let the block at index $i$ be the length-$B$ segment of $y$ beginning at position $iB$, truncated if necessary. Then the language of strings $z$ for which there exists an integer $i<a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$ such that the encoding of the pair consisting of $x$ and its block at index $i$ belongs to $V$ is in $\mathsf{P}$.
